data.cultural_impact: The name Shahdokht holds deep cultural significance in Persian tradition. Persian culture places a great emphasis on the majesty of the moon and its association with elegant beauty and serenity. The name Shahdokht, meaning "the lady of the moon," is a beautifully poetic way to capture the essence of the moon's enchanting allure in Persian literature and art. It represents the idea of hope and light that shines brightest in the darkest of times.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Shahdokht lies in its essence of illumination and wisdom. In Sufism, the Islamic mystic path, the moon is often symbolic of knowledge and spiritual enlightenment. Shahdokht, as the lady of the moon, is a reflection of the Holy Quranic verse, "And We have sent you (O Muhammad) with the truth as a bringer of good news and a warner. And there has come to you a belief from your Lord." (34:28). The name serves as a reminder of the importance of knowledge and wisdom in guiding us through the spiritual journey of life, especially in the face of challenges and darkness. It is a source of comfort and reassurance, reminding us of the power of light and knowledge to dispel the darkness and lead us towards the path of righteousness and spiritual growth.
